experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours typically include a cellar walk, explanation of the winemaking process, and a tasting flight of 4–6 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the most photographed sea caves in the world, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and sea arches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural scenery.

experiences.name: Lagos Old Town & Ponta da Piedade Sunset
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of Lagos historic center, visiting the 15th-century Igreja de Santa Maria and the old slave market museum. End the afternoon at Ponta da Piedade to watch the sunset illuminate the extraordinary golden rock formations and sea stacks from the clifftop viewpoint.
experiences.location: Lagos Old Town & Ponta da Piedade, Lagos

experiences.name: Tavira Island Beach Day & Local Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Take a short ferry to the pristine barrier island beach of Ilha de Tavira, part of the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Spend the morning on the unspoiled Atlantic-facing beach, then return to Tavira town for a traditional seafood lunch featuring grilled octopus, clams à Bulhão Pato, and a carafe of local Alentejo white wine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the affordable Aerobus or shared shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Algarve beachfront area (approx. €5-12). Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or petrol station near the resort. Pick up some local bread, cheese, and fruit to keep costs low on arrival night.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some euros handy for transport from the airport. Download the Rede Expressos or FlixBus app for future bus travel. Set an alarm and get a good night's rest — your Algarve adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first walk along the beachfront directly from Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the nearest beach (likely Meia Praia, Manta Rota, or local equivalent depending on exact resort location). Swim, relax, and soak in the golden Algarve morning sun. The beach is free and uncrowded in mid-September.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town centre on foot or by local bus (€1.50-2.50). Explore the local market or mercado municipal for fresh produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and pastries. Pick up supplies for budget picnic lunches throughout the trip. Visit the local church and main square for free sightseeing.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the promenade at sunset. Have dinner at a local tasca (traditional tavern) — look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) which typically costs €7-10 and includes bread, soup, main course, and sometimes a drink.

meals.breakfast: Café near the resort — order a galão (milky coffee) and a pastel de nata (custard tart) for under €2.50 total. Classic Portuguese breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market finds: local bread, queijo fresco (fresh cheese), presunto (cured ham), olives, and fruit. Total cost €4-6.
meals.dinner: Local tasca in town — prato do dia such as bacalhau à brás (shredded cod with eggs and potatoes) or grilled sardines with salad and bread. Budget €8-12 including a small local wine.

day_by_day.notes: September is shoulder season in Algarve — perfect weather (around 25-28°C), fewer crowds than August, and slightly lower prices. Always ask for the 'ementa turística' or daily menu for the best value at restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a bicycle (€10-15/day) to explore a nearby famous Algarve beach. Visit Praia da Marinha or Praia de Benagil (depending on your resort location) — some of the most stunning cliff-lined beaches in Europe. Arrive early to secure a good spot and enjoy the dramatic rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the clifftop trails (free) for breathtaking panoramic views of the coastline. The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) is a well-marked, free hiking trail offering spectacular scenery. Pack water and snacks from your market supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and visit a local supermarket (Lidl, Pingo Doce, or Continente) to pick up an affordable bottle of Alentejo or Algarve regional wine (€3-6). Enjoy a sunset wine session on your balcony or the beach before heading out for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Prepare breakfast in your room if kitchen facilities are available — yogurt, fruit, and local bread from the market. Otherwise, repeat the café galão and pastel de nata routine (€2.50).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic on the cliffs or beach — sandwiches with local deli meats, fruit, and water. Budget €3-5.
meals.dinner: Find a local cervejaria (beer hall/seafood restaurant) and order grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia) — typically €9-13. Share a jug of local sangria or order a small carafe of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the clifftop walk and bring plenty of sunscreen and water. The trails can be slippery near edges — stay on marked paths. Bus schedules may be limited in the afternoon, so check return times in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Take the regional train or Rede Expressos bus (€4-8 each way). Explore the old town walls, Slave Market Museum (€3 entry — one of the world's oldest slave trade sites), and the beautiful Igreja de Santo António.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a stunning headland with extraordinary golden rock formations, sea arches, and grottos. It's a free viewpoint accessible on foot from Lagos town centre (about 2km walk). Alternatively, take a short kayak or boat tour of the grottos (budget operators offer trips from €15-20).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' lively Rua 25 de Abril for affordable tapas bars and restaurants. The town has a great budget food scene. Head back to the resort by train or bus before the last service (usually around 21:00-22:00).

meals.breakfast: At the resort or a café near the bus/train station — toast with manteiga (butter) and local honey, plus coffee. €2-3.
meals.lunch: In Lagos — find a padaria (bakery) or local snack bar for a bifana (pork sandwich) or tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) for €2-4.
meals.dinner: Lagos tasca — try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew in a copper pot) if splitting with a travel companion, or opt for the affordable daily menu. Budget €10-14.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is very walkable. Wear comfortable shoes. The last train/bus back can fill up — check timetables on cp.pt (trains) or rede-expressos.pt (buses) and consider booking return in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local area around Aegean Bliss Resort more deeply. Visit any nearby fishing village or harbour — watch the local fishermen bring in the morning catch, browse the docks, and enjoy the authentic Algarve atmosphere. Many harbours have small fish markets open in the early morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience — visit a local Algarve wine producer or adega (winery). The Algarve wine region (DOC Algarve) is less famous than Alentejo but produces excellent wines. Look for cooperative wineries or smaller producers who offer free or low-cost tastings (€5-10 with a glass or two included). Adega do Cantor (near Guia) or local cooperative wineries are good budget options.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the beach for the golden hour. Cook a simple dinner in your room if kitchen facilities are available — buy fresh fish from the morning market and grill or bake it. Alternatively, enjoy a simple meal at a local snack bar.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and coffee at a local padaria — try a travesseiro (puff pastry with almond cream) or caracol (cinnamon roll). €2-3.
meals.lunch: At or near the winery — many offer light food pairings, or bring a picnic of local cheeses, bread, and cured meats to enjoy with your wine tasting. Budget €5-8 total.
meals.dinner: Self-catered fresh fish dinner in the room (if facilities available) — fresh sardines or sea bream from the market, grilled with olive oil, garlic, and lemon. Cost €5-8. Or visit a local snack bar for a simple meal under €10.

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm winery opening hours and whether tastings are available — some smaller producers require appointments. September is harvest season (vindima) in Portugal, which makes wine experiences especially authentic and atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the regional train (€3-5 each way — one of the most scenic rail routes in the Algarve). Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves and countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves' charming old town — visit the Gothic Sé Catedral (free entry), browse the local shops, and walk along the riverside. The town is far less touristy than Lagos or Albufeira, offering a more authentic experience at lower prices. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2 entry) for a glimpse into the region's history.
day_by_day.evening: Have an early dinner in Silves before catching the train back. The town has excellent, affordable traditional restaurants. Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxing evening walk along the beach.

meals.breakfast: At the resort or train station café — galão and tosta mista. €3.
meals.lunch: In Silves — find a local restaurant near the castle for a prato do dia. The inland Algarve is cheaper than the coast. Budget €7-9 for a full meal with drink.
meals.dinner: Early dinner in Silves before the return train — try frango piri-piri (piri-piri chicken) which is a local specialty, or grilled pork with migas (breadcrumb side dish). Budget €8-11.

day_by_day.notes: The train from the coast to Silves runs through beautiful orange and almond groves — sit on the right side for the best views. Check the return train schedule carefully as services can be infrequent in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Relax and recharge — spend the morning at the beach directly from Aegean Bliss Resort. Mid-trip rest day. Swim, sunbathe, read, and enjoy the beachfront location you're paying for. September sea temperatures in the Algarve are around 22-23°C — perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's immediate surroundings on foot. Look for any free local attractions — viewpoints (miradouros), small chapels, or natural areas. Many Algarve resorts are near walking trails through the natural park (Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina or Ria Formosa depending on location).
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to mark the halfway point of your trip — find a restaurant with a sea view and order fresh grilled fish. Still budget-conscious, but allow yourself a glass of local vinho verde or Algarve white wine.

meals.breakfast: Sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast — prepare fruit, yogurt, and local bread in the room, or visit a café for a full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, bread, and coffee. €4-6.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar near the resort — fresh grilled corn on the cob (milho assado), a bifana, or a simple salad. Budget €5-7.
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated budget dinner at a seafront restaurant — grilled dourada (sea bream) or robalo (sea bass) with potatoes and salad. Budget €14-18 including a glass of wine. Still excellent value.

day_by_day.notes: Use this rest day to do laundry if needed, recharge devices, plan the second half of the trip, and stock up on supplies at the supermarket. Check bus schedules for upcoming day trips.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Faro — the Algarve's capital city. Take the bus or train (€4-7 each way). Explore the historic Cidade Velha (Old Town) within the ancient walls — visit the Sé de Faro cathedral (€3.50, climb the tower for panoramic views), the Museu Municipal (€2), and the fascinating Igreja dos Ossos (Bone Chapel, €4).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Ria Formosa Natural Park waterfront — a stunning lagoon system with salt pans and birdlife. Take a short ferry to Ilha de Faro (€2.50 return) for a beautiful, less-crowded beach experience. The lagoon views are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's pedestrian shopping streets and have dinner before heading back. Faro has a good selection of budget-friendly restaurants catering to locals rather than tourists.

meals.breakfast: At the resort or on arrival in Faro at a local pastelaria. Try a queijada (cheese tart) — a local Algarve specialty. €2-3.
meals.lunch: In Faro's market hall (Mercado Municipal de Faro) — fresh produce stalls, snack bars, and local food at excellent prices. Try amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams in garlic and cilantro) as a starter if budget allows. €6-10.
meals.dinner: Faro restaurant near the marina — look for menus advertising 'menu turístico' at €10-13 for a 3-course meal with drink included.

day_by_day.notes: The Bone Chapel (Igreja dos Ossos) is a unique and sobering historical site — highly recommended. Faro airport is nearby if you need to confirm return flight details. Last buses/trains back to the resort area run until approximately 21:00-22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day — deeper dive into Algarve wines. Research and visit a second winery or arrange a guided wine tour of the region. The Algarve has four sub-regions: Lagos, Portimão, Lagoa, and Tavira. Lagoa is known for white wines. Look for cooperative wineries (adegas cooperativas) which offer the most affordable tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: After wine tasting, visit a nearby local beach for the afternoon. Enjoy the relaxed post-tasting glow with a swim and a nap on the sand. Bring a bottle of wine purchased at the winery (typically 20-30% cheaper than retail) to enjoy later.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by a casual dinner at a local snack bar or tasca. Keep it simple after the wine tasting afternoon — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) are perfect for sharing and grazing.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café — keep it light before wine tasting. Coffee and a pastry. €2.
meals.lunch: Many wineries offer light lunch options or food pairings — charcuterie, local cheeses, olives, and bread paired with wines. Budget €8-15 depending on the winery package.
meals.dinner: Petiscos dinner at a local tasca — order a variety of small plates: prego no pão (steak sandwich), chouriço assado (grilled chorizo), pataniscas de bacalhau (cod fritters), and a salad. Share and graze. Budget €10-14.

day_by_day.notes: Drink responsibly and stay hydrated during wine tastings — the Algarve sun is still strong in September. Designate a non-drinking navigator if renting a car. Many wineries are in rural areas and may require a taxi or pre-booked transport.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — often called the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Take the train (€3-6 each way). Explore this elegant town with its Roman bridge, castle ruins (free), whitewashed churches, and traditional four-sided rooftops. Visit the Tavira Island (Ilha de Tavira) ferry (€2 return) for a stunning natural beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on Ilha de Tavira — a barrier island beach accessible only by ferry, with crystal-clear water and a relaxed atmosphere. Much less crowded than the western Algarve beaches. Walk along the island's nature trails.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Tavira town before the return train. Tavira is known for excellent fresh seafood at very reasonable prices — it's a local town rather than a heavily touristy resort.

meals.breakfast: At the resort or Tavira train station café upon arrival. €2-3.
meals.lunch: Pack a light picnic for the island beach, or buy from the small beach café on Ilha de Tavira (simple snacks, €5-8).
meals.dinner: Tavira restaurant — try arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or grilled atum (tuna steak) — the eastern Algarve is famous for tuna. Budget €10-14 for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a gem that many tourists overlook in favour of the western Algarve. The town has a slower, more authentic pace. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs seasonally — confirm it's still operating in mid-September. Check last train back to your resort area.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at the resort — final days, so make the most of the beachfront location. Try a water sport if budget allows: stand-up paddleboarding (€10-15/hour) or bodyboarding (€5-8 board rental). Many beach operators offer morning deals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local farmers' market or weekly street market if one is running in the area (check local listings — markets rotate by day of the week across Algarve towns). Stock up on local products: almond sweets (amêndoas), carob products, local honey, and fig jam as affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner at your favourite restaurant from the trip — return to the best tasca you found and try something you haven't ordered yet. Toast to a wonderful trip with a glass of medronho (local arbutus berry spirit, similar to grappa) after dinner — often offered free by the house.

meals.breakfast: Special treat breakfast — visit a pastelaria and try a full selection of Portuguese pastries: pastel de nata, bola de berlim (cream-filled doughnut), and a galão. €4-5.
meals.lunch: Market lunch — graze on market food: fresh fruit, local cheese, olives, and bread. Budget €4-6.
meals.dinner: Return to your favourite restaurant — splurge slightly on a 3-course meal with a bottle of local wine to share. Budget €15-20 per person for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Start thinking about packing and logistics for departure. Check your flight details and arrange airport transport in advance. Lidl and Continente supermarkets are great for buying vacuum-packed local products (cheese, wine, olive oil) as affordable souvenirs within airline liquid/weight restrictions.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — one last sunrise beach walk directly from Aegean Bliss Resort. Reflect on the trip. Take photos of the resort and beach. If you haven't tried surfing or paddleboarding yet, this is your last chance. Alternatively, explore any nearby spot you haven't visited yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any remaining local sights — a chapel, viewpoint, or neighbourhood you noticed but didn't explore. Buy any remaining souvenirs: local wine bottles, almond products, or azulejo (decorative tile) magnets from local shops (€1-3 each).
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in the Algarve — keep it classic and affordable. Grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas) with boiled potatoes and salad is the quintessential Portuguese summer dish. Pair with local vinho verde. End the evening with a walk along the beach under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final resort breakfast or café visit. Try anything you haven't eaten yet — maybe a francesinha if you can find one, or local almond cake (tarte de amêndoa). €3-5.
meals.lunch: Light lunch — fresh salad, bread, and local cheese from the supermarket. Keep it simple as you begin to pack. Budget €3-5.
meals.dinner: Classic final dinner — grilled sardines or fresh catch of the day at a local tasca. Simple, affordable, and perfectly Portuguese. Budget €8-12 including wine or local beer.

day_by_day.notes: Pack tonight to make the morning easier. Keep airport transport costs in mind — book the Aerobus or shared shuttle in advance if your flight is early. Separate any liquids or oversized items for checked luggage. Leave a review for the resort if you enjoyed your stay!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy one last coffee and pastel de nata at a local café before departure. Take the Aerobus, shared shuttle, or local bus to Faro Airport (€5-15 depending on option). Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport time — browse duty-free for any last-minute Portuguese wine or products (Faro Airport has a good selection). Reflect on an amazing 13-day Algarve adventure: stunning beaches, excellent wines, fresh seafood, and authentic Portuguese culture — all on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry memories of golden cliffs, turquoise waters, local wine tastings, and incredible value Portuguese food back home.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a local café near the resort before checkout. €2-3.
meals.lunch: Light snack at Faro Airport — airport prices are higher, so bring any remaining snacks or pick up something simple. Budget €5-8.
meals.dinner: On the flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): €400-600 per person, covering transport (€80-120), meals (€200-280), activities and entrance fees (€50-80), wine tastings (€30-50), and miscellaneous/souvenirs (€40-70). The Algarve is one of Europe's best value destinations — you've made the most of every euro!

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival Day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area (approx. 30-45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and unwind at the resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the resort bar or a nearby 24-hour café if available. Try a Pastel de Nata and a glass of local Alentejo wine to start the Portuguese experience.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — nothing is scheduled before arrival. Confirm transfer booking in advance. Ask the resort front desk for a welcome orientation and local maps.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy your first full Algarve morning. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade near the resort. Explore the golden sandy beach, take a swim in the Atlantic, and soak in the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim. Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Pack snorkeling gear if available. The hike along the clifftop trail offers breathtaking views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower and change. Head into the nearest town center for a relaxed dinner at a traditional Portuguese tasca. Try grilled fish (Peixe Grelhado) or Cataplana de Marisco (seafood stew).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit, local cheese, bread, and a strong Portuguese espresso (Bica).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic or light snack at Praia da Marinha — grab fresh sandwiches, local olives, and water from a nearby deli or supermarket before heading out.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range local restaurant such as Restaurante O Alambique or similar tasca — budget approx. €20-30 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes for the Praia da Marinha trail. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — September sun in the Algarve is still strong. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local morning market (Mercado Municipal) in the nearest town to pick up fresh produce, local cheeses, smoked sausages, and Portuguese pastries. Immerse yourself in the daily rhythms of Algarve life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a taxi/bus to Lagos Old Town. Wander the cobblestone streets of Lagos' historic center, visiting the 15th-century Igreja de Santa Maria and the nearby Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos). Browse artisan shops and admire the Moorish-influenced architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for the famous Ponta da Piedade Sunset experience. Walk or take a short taxi to Ponta da Piedade to watch the sun set over the dramatic sea stacks and golden arches — one of the most iconic views in Portugal. Return to resort after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Lagos Old Town — try a casual café or snack bar. Order a Bifana (pork sandwich) or fresh grilled sardines with crusty bread. Budget approx. €10-15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Lagos at a mid-range restaurant near the marina. Try Arroz de Lingueirão (razor clam rice) or fresh grilled sea bass. Budget approx. €25-35 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 20-30 minutes from the Beachfront area by car. The Ponta da Piedade sunset is best around 7:30-8:00 PM in September — plan accordingly. Wear layers as evenings can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at the resort beach. Rent a paddleboard or kayak from a local beach operator. Explore the coastline from the water for a fresh perspective on the cliffs and coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Algarve winery for an afternoon wine tasting session. The Algarve wine region produces excellent reds and whites — look for estates near Lagoa or Silves such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and sample 4-6 wines paired with local charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a sundowner cocktail at the resort bar. Dine at the resort restaurant for a convenient and relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery — charcuterie board, local cheeses, bread, and olives paired with wine. Budget approx. €15-20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try the catch of the day or a local meat dish. Budget approx. €25-35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the winery tour in advance as September is harvest season (vindima) and tours fill up quickly. This is a fantastic time to visit — you may even witness grape harvesting in action.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) in the morning when it is less crowded. Explore the ramparts and enjoy panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves) and stroll through the charming town. Stop at a local cork shop — cork is a major Algarve product. In the afternoon, visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia to learn about the region's Moorish history.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the coast. Stop at a beachside restaurant for a casual seafood dinner as the sun goes down. Try percebes (barnacles) or amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in white wine and garlic).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at a local restaurant — try Frango Piri-Piri (spicy grilled chicken) or a hearty Caldo Verde soup. Budget approx. €12-18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront seafood restaurant on the way back — budget approx. €25-35 per person with local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 30-40 minutes inland from the coast. September is ideal for visiting as summer crowds have thinned. The castle entrance fee is approximately €3-5 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia de Benagil — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches. Take a boat tour from Benagil Beach into the spectacular Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil), a cathedral-like cave with a natural skylight. Book in advance as this is extremely popular.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat tour, relax on Benagil Beach or take a short coastal walk along the clifftop path. Visit nearby Praia de Carvalho, a hidden gem accessible via a short tunnel through the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a sunset swim at the resort beach followed by dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the Benagil beach snack bar or bring a packed lunch — fresh sandwiches, fruit, and cold drinks.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near the resort — try a Cataplana (traditional copper pot seafood dish). Budget approx. €25-30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave boat tours must be booked several days in advance in September. Tours typically run 45-60 minutes. Alternatively, experienced swimmers can swim into the cave from the beach at low tide — check conditions with locals first.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort — have a long breakfast, read by the pool, or get a spa treatment if the resort offers one. This is a mid-trip recharge day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle afternoon walk along the coastal cliffs near the resort. Discover hidden coves and viewpoints (miradouros) along the way. Bring a camera — the afternoon light on the golden limestone cliffs is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Venture into the nearest town for a wine bar experience. Visit a local adega or wine bar and try a selection of Algarve and Alentejo wines by the glass. Ask the sommelier for recommendations — look for Aragonez, Trincadeira, and Verdelho varieties.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort — try the full Portuguese spread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — salad, soup, or a club sandwich. Budget approx. €12-18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a wine bar restaurant in town — enjoy tapas-style petiscos (Portuguese tapas) paired with regional wines. Budget approx. €25-35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do laundry, recharge devices, and plan the second half of the trip. Check weather forecasts for upcoming days and adjust plans if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Sagres, at the southwestern tip of Portugal — one of the most dramatic and wind-swept landscapes in Europe. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress), where Henry the Navigator once planned his Age of Discovery voyages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. Stand at the edge of the continent and watch the waves crash against the 60-meter cliffs. Browse the small market stalls selling local honey, dried herbs, and handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Sagres village before driving back to the resort. Sagres is known for exceptional fresh fish — try the grilled tuna (atum) or swordfish (espadarte).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — pack some pastries for the road.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a casual café in Sagres — fresh fish soup (sopa de peixe) or a tosta mista with local coffee. Budget approx. €10-15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Sagres at a mid-range seafood restaurant near the harbor. Budget approx. €25-35 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 45-60 minutes west of Lagos. It can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The drive along the coast road (EN268) is scenic and worth taking slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the town of Portimão and its famous Praia da Rocha beach. Walk the 1.5km beach promenade and explore the dramatic rock formations at the eastern end of the beach. If the tide is right, explore the sea caves on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a river cruise or boat trip along the Arade River from Portimão marina. These 1-2 hour trips pass through beautiful countryside and offer a different perspective on the Algarve landscape. Alternatively, visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) — housed in a former canning factory, it tells the story of the sardine fishing industry.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its charcoal-grilled sardines — have dinner at one of the traditional restaurants along the riverside. This is a quintessential Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Praia da Rocha — salad, soup, or a snack. Budget approx. €10-15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Portimão at a traditional riverside restaurant — grilled sardines, piri-piri chicken, or fresh fish. Budget approx. €20-30 per person with house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is approximately 15-25 minutes from the resort area. The Portimão Museum is free on the first Sunday of the month. River cruise tickets cost approx. €15-25 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine day. Drive to the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve wine production. Visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa for a morning tour and tasting. The cooperative produces some of the finest Algarve wines and the tour includes the production facility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second winery — try Quinta da Penina or a nearby estate for a more boutique experience. Enjoy a vineyard walk, learn about the local grape varieties (Negra Mole, Crato Branco), and participate in a structured tasting with food pairing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort with a few bottles of your favorite discoveries. Enjoy a relaxed evening on the resort terrace with a glass of local wine and a light dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Winery lunch — most estates offer a wine and food pairing lunch. Budget approx. €20-30 per person.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort or a nearby casual restaurant — tapas, cheese board, and a bottle of your winery purchase. Budget approx. €20-25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to book both winery visits. September is harvest season — you may be able to participate in grape picking (vindima) for a small fee, which is a memorable experience. Purchase wine to take home — check airline liquid restrictions.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the eastern Algarve. Drive to Tavira, considered one of the most beautiful towns in the Algarve. Cross the Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visit the Tavira Castle ruins, and explore the 37 churches that dot this charming town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry or water taxi from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a barrier island with one of the most beautiful and unspoiled beaches in the Algarve. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and walking along the pristine shore. The water is calm and warm in September.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for dinner before driving back to the resort. Tavira is known for its excellent tuna dishes — try atum de cebolada (tuna with onions) or fresh grilled tuna steak.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — pack snacks for the day trip.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach snack bar on Ilha de Tavira — fresh fish, salads, and cold drinks. Budget approx. €15-20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Tavira at a riverside restaurant — budget approx. €25-35 per person with local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 60-75 minutes east of the resort. Start early to make the most of the day. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira costs approx. €2-3 per person return. The island has no cars — it is beautifully peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — return to your favorite beach discovered during the trip, or try a new one close to the resort. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the last full day in the Algarve sun. Take time to collect a few small shells or stones as natural souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan market or craft shop to pick up souvenirs — look for hand-painted azulejo tiles, cork products, local pottery, Algarve honey, and bottled wines. Spend the afternoon leisurely exploring the local area around the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant of the trip — treat yourself to a special meal. Consider a seafood Cataplana feast or a tasting menu at a slightly upscale local restaurant. Toast to an incredible 13-day Algarve adventure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café — keep it simple for the last full day. Budget approx. €12-18 per person.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a top-rated local restaurant — budget approx. €35-50 per person with a bottle of good Algarve or Alentejo wine.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight for an easier morning departure. Keep wine and fragile souvenirs in checked luggage wrapped in clothing. Leave a review for the Aegean Bliss Resort and any standout restaurants from the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast with views of the Algarve coastline. Take a short final walk on the beach to say goodbye to the Atlantic. Check out of the resort and transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, explore Faro itself if time allows — the Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha), the Arco da Vila, and the bone chapel at Igreja das Ossos are all worth a quick visit. Faro Airport is small and efficient — arrive 2 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry memories of golden cliffs, turquoise waters, exceptional wines, and warm Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort — savor every last Pastel de Nata.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Faro Airport or a café in Faro Old Town — budget approx. €10-15 per person.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow 30-45 minutes transfer time from the resort to Faro Airport. Confirm your flight details and check-in online the night before. The Algarve will be waiting for your return — September is truly one of the best months to visit.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours typically include a cellar walk, explanation of the winemaking process, and a tasting flight of 4–6 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the most photographed sea caves in the world, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and sea arches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural scenery.

experiences.name: Lagos Old Town & Ponta da Piedade Sunset
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of Lagos historic center, visiting the 15th-century Igreja de Santa Maria and the old slave market museum. End the afternoon at Ponta da Piedade to watch the sunset illuminate the extraordinary golden rock formations and sea stacks from the clifftop viewpoint.
experiences.location: Lagos Old Town & Ponta da Piedade, Lagos

experiences.name: Tavira Island Beach Day & Local Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Take a short ferry to the pristine barrier island beach of Ilha de Tavira, part of the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Spend the morning on the unspoiled Atlantic-facing beach, then return to Tavira town for a traditional seafood lunch featuring grilled octopus, clams à Bulhão Pato, and a carafe of local Alentejo white wine.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort whisks you directly to the hotel. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity (chilled local wine, artisan cheese board) prepared by the resort, and settle in for the night.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light welcome amenity in-room: regional Algarve charcuterie, queijo de figo (fig & almond cheese), and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine courtesy of the resort

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort. Confirm late check-in with the concierge. Unpack and rest — the adventure begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast with ocean views. Spend the late morning exploring the Aegean Bliss Resort's private beachfront — take a gentle swim in the calm September Atlantic waters, settle into a premium sun lounger, and get acquainted with the resort's beach butler service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. A private guide leads you along the dramatic golden limestone cliffs of one of the Algarve's most celebrated coastlines. Swim in crystal-clear coves, explore hidden sea arches, and photograph the iconic rock formations. The September light is spectacular and crowds are thinner than peak summer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail at the beachfront bar. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, requesting a terrace table overlooking the sea.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet featuring fresh pastéis de nata, tropical fruits, smoked salmon, regional cheeses, and freshly squeezed orange juice — included with your stay
meals.lunch: Private picnic basket arranged by the resort concierge, enjoyed atop the cliffs at Praia da Marinha — sourdough sandwiches, local olives, chilled rosé, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: Begin with percebes (barnacles) and amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in white wine & garlic), followed by grilled robalo (sea bass) with cataplana-style vegetables, paired with a bottle of Algarve Vida Nova white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Praia da Marinha guided hike in advance through the concierge. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring water shoes for the rocky coves. September water temperature is approximately 22°C — ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. A luxury small-group or private guide takes you by kayak through the world-famous Benagil Cave — a stunning domed sea cave with a natural skylight. The September conditions offer calmer seas and fewer crowds. Explore surrounding grottos and sea stacks along this legendary stretch of coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and enjoy the infinity pool overlooking the ocean. Book a 90-minute couple's massage or deep-tissue treatment at the resort spa — the perfect recovery after a morning of paddling.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private balcony with the Atlantic as your backdrop. Dine at a nearby premium restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagoa village.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly baked almond croissants, açorda (traditional bread soup), smoked Alentejo sausage, and specialty Portuguese coffee
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at A Cozinha do Mar (or equivalent upscale seafood restaurant near Benagil/Carvoeiro): grilled tiger prawns, fresh bread with olive oil, and a cold Sagres Bohemia beer or local vinho verde
meals.dinner: Restaurant Bon Bon (Michelin-starred, Carvoeiro area): tasting menu featuring modern Portuguese cuisine with Algarve seasonal ingredients — reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Book Benagil kayak as a private tour for the most exclusive experience. Depart early morning (8:00–9:00 AM) to catch the best cave lighting and avoid afternoon winds. Confirm spa appointments with resort 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated resort morning — enjoy a private yoga or stretching session on the beach arranged by the resort wellness team. Then take a long, unhurried swim along the resort's private beach before a late, indulgent breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour. A chauffeured private car takes you to Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar and/or Adega do Cantor near Guia (Cliff Richard's celebrated winery). Enjoy guided cellar tours, barrel tastings, and a curated flight of regional reds, whites, and the distinctive Algarve Vida Nova rosé. Learn about the unique terroir of the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in the late afternoon. Enjoy a private wine-pairing dinner in your suite or on your terrace, featuring bottles selected during the day's vineyard tour.

meals.breakfast: Late resort breakfast on your private terrace — eggs Benedict with smoked Alentejo ham, freshly squeezed blood orange juice, and a cheese board
meals.lunch: Vineyard lunch at Quinta dos Vales estate restaurant: charcuterie platters, local cheeses, fig jam, fresh bread, and estate olive oil paired with wine tastings
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining arranged by the resort: cataplana de marisco (seafood stew in a traditional copper pot) with crusty bread, paired with a premium bottle of Quinta dos Vales Grande Reserva red

day_by_day.notes: Book the private vineyard tour and chauffeur through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Request an English-speaking sommelier guide at the wineries. Purchase a selection of wines to take home — the resort can arrange shipping.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk along the resort's beachfront. After breakfast, explore the charming coastal town of Ferragudo (a short drive or boat transfer away) — a picturesque fishing village with a medieval castle, colorful boats, and whitewashed houses draped in bougainvillea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Charter a private luxury yacht or catamaran for an afternoon cruise along the Algarve coast. Sail past sea caves, golden cliffs, and hidden beaches. Snorkel in pristine coves, enjoy on-board canapés and champagne, and anchor at a secluded beach accessible only by sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort and freshen up. Dine at one of the Algarve's most celebrated seafood restaurants in Portimão or the marina area.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — traditional Portuguese açorda de marisco (seafood bread soup), fresh pastries, tropical fruit platter, and galão coffee
meals.lunch: On-board private yacht catering: chilled oysters, smoked salmon blinis, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and a bottle of Moët & Chandon Brut or local sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo) or equivalent premium marina restaurant: whole grilled dourada (sea bream) baked in sea salt, with roasted vegetables and a crisp Algarve white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book private yacht charter at least 3–4 days in advance through the resort concierge or a local charter company. September weather is typically calm — ideal for sailing. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a light layer for the evening on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed resort morning — enjoy the resort's private beach, take a paddleboard lesson with the resort's water sports team, or simply lounge by the infinity pool with a good book and fresh juice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos Old Town & Ponta da Piedade at sunset. A private driver takes you to Lagos, where you wander the cobblestone streets of the historic 15th-century center, visit the Igreja de Santa Maria and the haunting Mercado de Escravos (slave market museum). Then head to Ponta da Piedade for the most dramatic golden-hour coastal scenery in the Algarve — towering amber rock formations, grottos, and turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Ponta da Piedade. Dine in Lagos at a premium restaurant before returning to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Resort Sunday brunch special — eggs royale, avocado toast with Algarve olive oil, acai bowls, and a Bloody Mary or fresh green juice
meals.lunch: Light resort poolside lunch: grilled halloumi salad, fresh seafood tartare, and a chilled glass of vinho verde
meals.dinner: No Pátio (Lagos) or Restaurante Adega da Marina: Begin with tuna tataki with ponzu, followed by traditional arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) and a bottle of Esporão Reserva white

day_by_day.notes: Visit Ponta da Piedade around 6:30–7:00 PM for the best golden hour light in September. Consider hiring a small boat at the base of the cliffs to explore the sea caves from the water — a magical experience at sunset. Book the private driver for the round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip wellness morning — book a full spa half-day package at the resort: sauna, steam room, hydrotherapy pool, and a signature Algarve-inspired treatment using local carob and almond oils. Follow with a mindful beach walk and a light swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private cooking class arranged by the resort or a local culinary studio. Learn to prepare iconic Algarve dishes: cataplana de peixe, pastéis de nata, and amêijoas à Bulhão Pato. A local chef guides you through the market (if available) and the kitchen.
day_by_day.evening: Dine on the meal you prepared during the cooking class, served on your private terrace with a curated wine pairing selected by the resort sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-spa breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and almonds, fresh fruit, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-spa resort poolside lunch: seared tuna salad niçoise, artisan bread with tapenade, and a glass of chilled Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations — cataplana de peixe, fresh clams, and homemade pastéis de nata for dessert — served on your private terrace with a bottle of Quinta dos Vales white

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa half-day package and cooking class through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. The cooking class can typically be arranged as a private 2-person experience for couples. This is a wonderful mid-trip reset day.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for Tavira Island Beach Day & Local Seafood Lunch. A private chauffeured transfer takes you east along the Algarve coast to Tavira (approximately 1 hour). Take the short ferry to Ilha de Tavira, a pristine barrier island within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The beach is wide, unspoiled, and far quieter in September than in peak summer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a long, luxurious morning on Ilha de Tavira's beach, return to the town of Tavira for lunch at a premium seafood restaurant. Explore Tavira's charming historic center — the Roman bridge, Moorish castle ruins, and the distinctive four-sloped rooftops unique to this region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private transfer. Enjoy a quiet evening — sunset cocktails at the resort bar and a light dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast to go — a packed gourmet breakfast box: almond pastries, fruit, cheese, and a thermos of coffee for the journey
meals.lunch: Restaurante Quatro Águas (Tavira) — one of the Algarve's finest seafood restaurants: grilled linguado (sole), fresh oysters from the Ria Formosa, and a bottle of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Light resort dinner: fresh burrata with heirloom tomatoes, grilled octopus salad, and a glass of Algarve Vida Nova rosé on the terrace

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Ilha de Tavira run regularly and take only 5 minutes. Rent sun loungers and an umbrella on the island. September is perfect — warm sun, calm sea, and far fewer visitors than July/August. Bring cash for the ferry (small amount).

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour day — this time focusing on a different producer. Visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's Vida Nova estate near Guia) if not visited on Day 4, or explore a boutique family-run quinta in the Serra de Monchique hills. Enjoy a private tasting session with the winemaker and a tour of the vineyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the vineyard, visit the Caldas de Monchique spa village in the foothills of the Serra de Monchique — a beautiful, cool, forested retreat with natural thermal springs. Stroll the shaded gardens and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere, a refreshing contrast to the coastal heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a premium dinner at a nearby fine-dining establishment or the resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked salmon on sourdough, scrambled eggs with truffle, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at the vineyard: traditional Alentejo-style spread — bread, olive oil, local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), and estate wine pairings
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining restaurant: seven-course tasting menu with wine pairing — featuring seasonal Algarve ingredients including figs, almonds, carob, and fresh Atlantic seafood

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique offers a cool, lush microclimate — bring a light layer. The thermal waters at Caldas de Monchique have been celebrated since Roman times. Book the vineyard visit and private winemaker session in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach and water sports morning at the resort. Try a private stand-up paddleboard tour along the coastline, a guided snorkel session in a nearby cove, or simply relax on the resort's private beach with the beach butler service — chilled towels, fresh juices, and sun lounger setup included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Silves Medieval Castle — one of the best-preserved Moorish fortresses in Portugal, located about 30 minutes inland. Explore the red sandstone battlements, the archaeological museum, and the charming market town below. Silves was once the Moorish capital of the Algarve and is rich in history.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves or return to the resort for a romantic private beach dinner arranged by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Portuguese spread: fresh orange juice, pastéis de nata, regional cheeses, cured meats, and galão coffee
meals.lunch: Café Inglês (Silves) — a beloved terrace restaurant within the castle walls: fresh salads, grilled chicken piri-piri, and local wine
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner arranged by the resort: a table set on the sand with lanterns, a personalized menu of grilled seafood and local wines, and a dedicated waiter — the ultimate Algarve luxury experience

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private beach dinner at least 48–72 hours in advance with the resort concierge — this is one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Silves is best visited in the afternoon when the light on the red castle walls is stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise walk on the beach followed by a resort spa treatment — try the signature Algarve carob body wrap or a deep-tissue sports massage. After the treatment, enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast on your private terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ria Formosa Natural Park by private boat. This UNESCO-listed lagoon system stretches 60km along the Algarve coast and is one of Portugal's most important natural treasures. A private boat tour takes you through the waterways, past flamingos, herons, and sea horses, stopping at hidden sandbars and remote beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a final elegant dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a celebration of the Algarve's finest flavors.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast on your terrace: eggs Benedict with smoked tuna, fresh figs with local honey, almond cake, and a glass of chilled cava
meals.lunch: On-board private boat lunch: fresh oysters from the Ria Formosa, cold cuts, artisan bread, and chilled white wine enjoyed on the water
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — final tasting menu: amuse-bouche of local fish roe, percebes, lobster bisque, grilled turbot with algae butter, Algarve almond tart, and a premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Ria Formosa boat tour through the resort or a specialist operator in Faro or Olhão. September is excellent for birdwatching — flamingos are often present. Bring binoculars if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — make the most of the resort's private beachfront. Take a long swim, order fresh coconut water and acai bowls from the beach butler, and simply absorb the Algarve's golden September light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming market town of Loulé — the Algarve's inland cultural capital. Visit the covered Moorish-arched market hall (Mercado de Loulé), browse artisan shops selling hand-painted azulejos, cork goods, and local crafts, and visit the medieval castle. This is the perfect afternoon for picking up premium souvenirs and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a farewell dinner — either at the resort or at a celebrated nearby restaurant. Toast to an extraordinary 13 days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — the works: smoked salmon, eggs any style, pastries, fruit, cheeses, and your favorite Portuguese coffee
meals.lunch: Restaurante Bica Velha (Loulé) — a beloved traditional restaurant in a historic building: pork with clams (carne de porco à Alentejana), fresh bread, and local wine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Vila Joya (Albufeira) — one of Portugal's most celebrated Michelin two-star restaurants: a multi-course tasting menu with exceptional wine pairing. Reserve weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya requires reservations far in advance and has a formal dress code — smart elegant attire required. This is the culinary highlight of the trip. The Loulé market is best visited on Saturday morning when it is most vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the resort's private beach. Enjoy a last, leisurely resort breakfast with ocean views. Pack, settle the bill, and take one final dip in the ocean or the infinity pool. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either relax at the resort until transfer time or make a final stop at a nearby beach café or wine shop in Faro for last-minute purchases. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport, carrying memories of 13 extraordinary days of beaches, wine, golden cliffs, and the very best of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a celebratory spread: Champagne mimosas, eggs royale, fresh pastéis de nata, local cheeses, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a café near Faro Airport or the resort: bifanas (pork sandwiches), fresh pastries, and a last galão coffee
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer with the resort at least 24 hours before departure. Allow extra time at Faro Airport for security, especially on busy Sunday departures in September. Consider purchasing Algarve wines, local honey, carob products, and hand-painted ceramics as gifts before departure.
